claim: DSCAM and DSCAML1 have canonical PDZ-interacting motifs at their C-termini by which they interact with scaffolding proteins in the MAGI (membrane-associated guanylate kinase with inverted orientation) and PSD95 families.
source: Both DSCAM and DSCAML1 also have canonical PDZ-interacting motifs at their C-termini by which they interact with scaffolding proteins in the MAGI (membrane-associated guanylate kinase with inverted orientation) and PSD95 families (Yamagata and Sanes, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yamagata and Sanes, 2010, which provides published evidence for this interaction.

claim: The deletion of the C-terminal 10 amino acids disrupts the canonical binding to the hydrophobic pocket of PDZ domains.
source: Deletion of these final 10 amino acids disrupts the canonical binding to the hydrophobic pocket of PDZ domains (Doyle et al., 1996), and this DSCAM-∆C mutation markedly reduced MAGI-3 association in co-immunoprecipitation experiments with the DSCAM intracellular domain (ICD) when co-transfected in HEK293T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Doyle et al., 1996, and by experimental data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating reduced MAGI-3 association.

claim: DscamΔC/ΔC mice survived without hydrocephaly or any of the overt phenotypes observed in null animals.
source: Unlike null mutants, which do not survive on a C57BL/6 background, DscamΔC/ΔC mice survived without hydrocephaly or any of the overt phenotypes observed in null animals (Amano et al., 2009; Fuerst et al., 2010, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to null mutants described in cited references and by observation of the DscamΔC/ΔC mice.

claim: The relative abundance and size of DSCAM protein was indistinguishable between Dscam+/+ and DscamΔC/ΔC samples.
source: The relative abundance and size of DSCAM protein was indistinguishable between Dscam+/+ and DscamΔC/ΔC samples, while negative control Dscam-/- samples were devoid of DSCAM protein, as expected (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C comparing protein levels across genotypes.

claim: At three weeks of age, there was no obvious mislocalization or reduction in labeling in cryosections from DscamΔC/ΔC retinas labeled for DSCAM by immunofluorescence.
source: At three weeks of age, there was no obvious mislocalization or reduction in labeling in cryosections from DscamΔC/ΔC retinas labeled for DSCAM by immunofluorescence (Figure 1D–F, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1D-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: DscamΔC/ΔC retinas showed some expansion and disorganization, but a milder phenotype than in Dscam-/- animals.
source: DscamΔC/ΔC retinas showed some expansion and disorganization, but a milder phenotype than in Dscam-/- animals (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological comparison shown in Figure 1H.

claim: DA cells had a significant increase in cell density and a loss of mosaic spacing in Dscam∆C/∆C mice.
source: DA cells had a significant increase in cell density and a loss of mosaic spacing in Dscam∆C/∆C mice (Figure 2D–G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell density and spacing shown in Figure 2D-G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: By all measures, DA cell organization in Dscam∆C/∆C retinas was indistinguishable from that of Dscam-/- mice.
source: By all measures, DA cell organization in Dscam∆C/∆C retinas was indistinguishable from that of Dscam-/- mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison of multiple spacing measures (DRP, Voronoi, nearest neighbor) shown in Figure 2.

claim: bNOS-positive amacrine cells in Dscam∆C/∆C mice showed little, if any, disruption in organization.
source: Conversely, bNOS-positive amacrine cells in Dscam∆C/∆C mice showed little, if any, disruption in organization.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell spacing and density shown in Figure 2K-N.

claim: bNOS-positive amacrine cells maintained a clear exclusion zone in Dscam∆C/∆C mice, and were not significantly different from wildtype controls by any spacing measure.
source: bNOS-positive amacrine cells maintained a clear exclusion zone in Dscam∆C/∆C mice, and were not significantly different from wildtype controls by any spacing measure, nor did their overall cell density differ from controls (Figure 2K–N, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2K-N and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ipRGCs are among the most clustered and fasciculated cell types in Dscam-/- mutants.
source: ipRGCs are among the most clustered and fasciculated cell types in Dscam-/- mutants; both M1 and M2 cells are severely clustered with tight dendritic fascicles (Figure 3A,C, and [Fuerst et al., 2009]).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data in Figure 3A,C and by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: In Dscam∆C/∆C mutants, ipRGC cell bodies were clearly clustered, albeit not as severely as in Dscam-/- mice.
source: In Dscam∆C/∆C mutants, cell bodies were clearly clustered, albeit not as severely as in Dscam-/- mice (Figure 3B,E–G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3B,E-G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ipRGC cell density appeared to be modestly increased compared to controls, but the difference was not statistically significant.
source: Cell density appeared to be modestly increased compared to controls, but the difference was not statistically significant (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cdh3-GFP RGC cell number was not significantly increased in DscamΔC/ΔC retinas.
source: In contrast, cell number was not significantly increased in DscamΔC/ΔC retinas, and the cell body clustering observed in Dscam-/- mutants was not observed (Figure 3I,K–N, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3I,K-N and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The cell body clustering observed in Dscam-/- mutants was not observed in DscamΔC/ΔC retinas for Cdh3-GFP RGCs.
source: In contrast, cell number was not significantly increased in DscamΔC/ΔC retinas, and the cell body clustering observed in Dscam-/- mutants was not observed (Figure 3I,K–N, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 3I,K-N and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dscaml1 is expressed in the cells that contribute to the rod circuit, including rod photoreceptors, rod bipolar cells (RBCs), and AII amacrine cells.
source: Dscaml1 is expressed in the cells that contribute to the rod circuit, including rod photoreceptors, rod bipolar cells (RBCs), and AII amacrine cells (Fuerst et al., 2009), as well as a population of previously undefined cells in the inner nuclear layer.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: DSCAML1-∆C protein had the expected membrane topology, but did not co-immunoprecipitate with MAGI-3.
source: DSCAML1-∆C protein had the expected membrane topology, but did not co-immunoprecipitate with MAGI-3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas were modestly expanded, but not so severely as in Dscaml1-/- mutants.
source: Like Dscam, Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas were modestly expanded, but not so severely as in Dscaml1-/- mutants (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological comparison shown in Figure 4B-D.

claim: There was no increase in AII amacrine cell density in Dscaml1∆C/∆C animals.
source: There was no increase in cell density, and cells did not form clusters in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice, as they did in Dscaml1-/- animals, as measured by DRP or nearest neighbor analysis (Figure 4H,I,K).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4H,I,K.

claim: AII amacrine cells did not form clusters in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice, as they did in Dscaml1-/- animals.
source: There was no increase in cell density, and cells did not form clusters in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice, as they did in Dscaml1-/- animals, as measured by DRP or nearest neighbor analysis (Figure 4H,I,K).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4H,I,K.

claim: There was an increased covariance of Voronoi tessellation domain areas compared to controls for AII amacrine cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice.
source: There was, however, an increased covariance of Voronoi tessellation domain areas compared to controls (Figure 4J, Figure 4—figure supplement 2) indicative of irregular spacing.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4J and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: VGLUT3-positive amacrine cell number was significantly increased in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice.
source: Cell number was significantly increased, and DRP, Voronoi, and nearest neighbor analyses all indicated a significant loss of mosaic spacing (Figure 4O–R, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4O-R and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice showed a significant loss of mosaic spacing.
source: Cell number was significantly increased, and DRP, Voronoi, and nearest neighbor analyses all indicated a significant loss of mosaic spacing (Figure 4O–R, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4O-R and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: ipRGCs were more severely clustered in Dscam∆C/∆C than in Bax-/- animals, as measured by DRP packing factor and Voronoi domain analysis.
source: ipRGCs were more severely clustered in Dscam∆C/∆C than in Bax-/- animals, as measured by DRP packing factor (Figure 5B) and Voronoi domain analysis (Figure 5C), but were not significantly different by nearest neighbor analysis (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: DA cell spacing was similarly disrupted in Bax-/- mutants as in Dscam∆C/∆C.
source: DA cell spacing was similarly disrupted in Bax-/-mutants as in Dscam∆C/∆C (Figure 5F–H), while VGLUT3-positive cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C were significantly more disrupted by Voronoi and nearest neighbor analyses, but not by DRP packing factor, despite a significantly lower cell density than Bax-/- retinas (Figure 5I–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5F-H.

claim: VGLUT3-positive cell spacing in Dscaml1∆C/∆C was more severely disrupted than could be explained by increased cell number alone.
source: while VGLUT3-positive cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C were significantly more disrupted by Voronoi and nearest neighbor analyses, but not by DRP packing factor, despite a significantly lower cell density than Bax-/- retinas (Figure 5I–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5I-L comparing Dscaml1∆C/∆C to Bax-/- retinas.

claim: DA neurites were not severely fasciculated in Bax-/- mutants.
source: However, we observed that the DA neurites were not severely fasciculated in Bax-/- mutants (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: There was significantly more severe fasciculation in Dscam∆C/∆C and Dscam-/- retinas than in controls or Bax-/- retinas for DA cells.
source: For DA cells, there was significantly more severe fasciculation in Dscam∆C/∆C and Dscam-/- retinas than in controls or Bax-/- retinas (Figure 6A–D,M).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Elo scoring shown in Figure 6M.

claim: In the ON layer (predominantly M2 cells), the Elo score could not distinguish Dscam∆C/∆C retinas from control or from Bax-/- retinas.
source: The Elo score could not distinguish Dscam∆C/∆C retinas from control or from Bax-/- retinas, but Dscam-/- fasciculation was significantly more severe than in all other genotypes (Figure 6G,N).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Elo scoring shown in Figure 6N.

claim: In the OFF layer (predominantly M1 cells), by Elo score Dscam∆C/∆C retinas were intermediately fasciculated between control and Dscam-/- but were indistinguishable from Bax-/- mutants.
source: Indeed, by Elo score Dscam∆C/∆C retinas were intermediately fasciculated between control and Dscam-/- but were indistinguishable from Bax-/- mutants (Figure 6O).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Elo scoring shown in Figure 6O.

claim: Cdh3-GFP RGC dendrites had tight fasciculation in Dscam-/- mutants, but no discernable difference between DscamΔC/ΔC and control retinas.
source: We also assessed the fasciculation of Cdh3-GFP RGC dendrites and found tight fasciculation in Dscam-/- mutants, but no discernable difference between DscamΔC/ΔC and control retinas (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Elo scoring shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: bNOS-positive amacrine cells had mild fasciculation, if any, in DscamΔC/ΔC and Bax-/- mutants.
source: Similarly, bNOS-positive amacrine cells had mild fasciculation, if any, in DscamΔC/ΔC and Bax-/- mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Elo scoring shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: bNOS-positive amacrine cells stratified normally in Dscam∆C/∆C retinas.
source: We inspected bNOS-positive amacrine stratification in Dscam∆C/∆C retinas, which are on a C57BL/6 background, and found no abnormalities (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: DA cell and M1 ipRGCs co-stratify correctly in the OFF region of the IPL in Dscam∆C/∆C mutants.
source: DA cell and M1 ipRGCs co-stratify correctly in the OFF region of the IPL in Dscam-/- mutants (Fuerst et al., 2009), and both correctly targeted in Dscam∆C/∆C mutants as well (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7C-D and by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: There is a clear co-fasciculation between DA cells and M1 ipRGCs in Dscam∆C/∆C mutants.
source: Interestingly, there is a clear co-fasciculation between these cell types in Dscam∆C/∆C mutants (Figure 7E), suggesting that the M1 fasciculation may be influenced by the DA cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: AII amacrine cells and rod bipolar cells terminate their processes normally in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mutants.
source: In Dscaml1-/- mutants, stratification and synaptic pairing between rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells is preserved (Fuerst et al., 2009). We found that to be the case in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice as well: both cell types project to the ON region of the IPL adjacent to the RGL (Figure 7F–I) where they connect at dyad synapses.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7F-I and by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: Dyad synapses in Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas did not display the synaptic phenotype reminiscent of the Dscaml1-/- mice.
source: We inspected the dyad synapses in Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas by transmission electron microscopy, and failed to detect these synaptic phenotype reminiscent of the Dscaml1-/- mice (Figure 7L–M), indicating that DSCAML1 promotes synapse maturation independent of C-terminal interactions.
evidence: The claim is supported by TEM analysis shown in Figure 7L-M.

claim: In Dscaml1∆C/∆C mutants, some VGLUT3-positive amacrine neurites projected past the ON ChAT band into the region where AII amacrines and RBCs target.
source: We found that in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mutants, some of these neurites projected past the ON ChAT band into the region where AII amacrines and RBCs target (Figure 7O).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7O.

claim: Much of the VGLUT3 labeling below the ON ChAT band was directly adjacent to Dab1-positive AII amacrine terminals in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mutants.
source: Indeed, much of the VGLUT3 labeling below the ON ChAT band was directly adjacent to Dab1-positive AII amacrine terminals (Figure 7P), an association that persisted through adulthood (18 months, Figure 7Q).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7P-Q.

claim: VGLUT3 occupied a significantly greater percentage of area in Dscaml1∆C/∆C animals than in controls.
source: VGLUT3 occupied a significantly greater percentage of area in Dscaml1∆C/∆C animals than in controls (2-way ANOVA, p<0.0001, Figure 7R).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 7R.

claim: Some cell types developed almost normally in the absence of PDZ-interacting C-termini, while others resembled complete loss of function.
source: Instead, we found that in the absence of these interactions, some cell types developed almost normally, while others resembled complete loss of function.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants as described throughout the Results section.

claim: Different cell types have different dependencies on the PDZ-interacting C-termini of Dscams for function.
source: Thus, we show differential dependence on this domain for Dscams' functions in different cell types.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants as described throughout the Results section.

claim: The vertebrate retina provides an advantageous model to study how specific neuronal cell types organize themselves during development to form functional circuits.
source: The vertebrate retina provides an advantageous model to study how specific neuronal cell types organize themselves during development to form functional circuits.
evidence: This is a general statement about the retina as a model system, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The ~100 neuronal cell types of the retina vertically organize into layers.
source: The ~100 neuronal cell types of the retina vertically organize into layers, with light-transducing photoreceptors in the outermost cellular layer (ONL, or outer nuclear layer) and retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) – responsible for the sole output from the retina – in the innermost layer (RGL, or retinal ganglion cell layer).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about retinal organization, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Many cell types are horizontally spaced in a mosaic pattern, such that there is a low probability of finding two neurons of the same subtype in close proximity.
source: Additionally, many cell types are horizontally spaced in a mosaic pattern, such that there is a low probability of finding two neurons of the same subtype (i.e., homotypic) in close proximity. This pattern ensures that the information processing provided by each subtype is distributed across the retina (Masland, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Masland, 2012.

claim: Dscam and Dscaml1 encode homophilic members of the Ig-superfamily of cell adhesion molecules.
source: Dscam and Dscaml1 encode homophilic members of the Ig-superfamily of cell adhesion molecules, and are expressed in non-overlapping neuronal subtypes in the retina (Agarwala et al., 2001; Fuerst et al., 2009; Yamagata and Sanes, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Agarwala et al., 2001; Fuerst et al., 2009; Yamagata and Sanes, 2008.

claim: Dscam and Dscaml1 are expressed in non-overlapping neuronal subtypes in the retina.
source: Dscam and Dscaml1 encode homophilic members of the Ig-superfamily of cell adhesion molecules, and are expressed in non-overlapping neuronal subtypes in the retina (Agarwala et al., 2001; Fuerst et al., 2009; Yamagata and Sanes, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Agarwala et al., 2001; Fuerst et al., 2009; Yamagata and Sanes, 2008.

claim: When either Dscam or Dscaml1 is mutated, the cell types that normally express the Dscam lose their mosaic spacing and often form clusters.
source: The Dscams promote self-avoidance at the cell type level: When either gene is mutated, the cell types that normally express the Dscam lose their mosaic spacing and often form clusters (Fuerst et al., 2009, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fuerst et al., 2009, 2008.

claim: Self-avoidance requires homophilic Dscam interactions between cells.
source: Self-avoidance requires homophilic Dscam interactions between cells, demonstrated in mosaic experiments where neurons lacking Dscam fasciculate with homotypic neurons with intact Dscam (Fuerst et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2012.

claim: Dscam1 in Drosophila promotes self-avoidance at the individual cell level by using alternative splicing to produce 19,008 distinctly homophilic isoforms.
source: Most notably, Dscam1 promotes self-avoidance at the individual cell level by using alternative splicing to produce 19,008 distinctly homophilic isoforms, allowing each neuron to recognize and avoid 'self' while still interacting with 'non-self' during processes like dendrite arborization and axon branching (reviewed in [Zipursky and Grueber, 2013]).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zipursky and Grueber, 2013.

claim: In Dscam and Dscaml1 mutant mice, there is an overabundance of each affected cell type, resulting in a severe expansion of the retina through the cellular and plexiform layers.
source: Dscams are also required for normal developmental cell death. In the mutant mice, there is an overabundance of each affected cell type, resulting in a severe expansion of the retina through the cellular and plexiform layers.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data presented in the manuscript and by citations to previous work.

claim: The extent of cell number expansion varies with cell type in Dscam and Dscaml1 mutants.
source: The extent of cell number expansion varies with cell type. Some cell types are expanded beyond even that seen in mutants for the pro-apoptotic Bax gene, while others are more modestly expanded compared to Bax mutants (Fuerst et al., 2009, 2008; Keeley et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fuerst et al., 2009, 2008; Keeley et al., 2012.

claim: In chick, Dscams label-specific sublaminae of the IPL and can instruct neurite targeting to these layers.
source: In chick, Dscams label-specific sublaminae of the IPL and can instruct neurite targeting to these layers (Yamagata and Sanes, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Yamagata and Sanes, 2008.

claim: DSCAM protein localization is punctate throughout the IPL in mouse, and is not confined to specific sublaminae.
source: DSCAM protein localization is punctate throughout the IPL in mouse, and is not confined to specific sublaminae (de Andrade et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to de Andrade et al., 2014.

claim: Some neuronal types have disorganized neurite stratification in Dscam mutants, although the disorganization varies with genetic background.
source: Despite this, some neuronal types do have disorganized neurite stratification in Dscam mutants, although the disorganization varies with genetic background (Fuerst et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2010.

claim: Dyad ribbon synapses between rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells can still be found in Dscaml1 mutants, but are morphologically abnormal, with indistinct, detached presynaptic ribbons.
source: For instance, Dscaml1 is expressed both in rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells, which connect at dyad ribbon synapses in the IPL. These synapses can still be found in Dscaml1 mutants, but are morphologically abnormal, with indistinct, detached presynaptic ribbons, and functionally abnormal, with much slower decay of the synaptic current (Fuerst et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: Dyad ribbon synapses between rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells in Dscaml1 mutants are functionally abnormal, with much slower decay of the synaptic current.
source: For instance, Dscaml1 is expressed both in rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells, which connect at dyad ribbon synapses in the IPL. These synapses can still be found in Dscaml1 mutants, but are morphologically abnormal, with indistinct, detached presynaptic ribbons, and functionally abnormal, with much slower decay of the synaptic current (Fuerst et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: Signaling molecules have been found in complex with Dscam1 in Drosophila (e.g., Dock/Pak, Ableson, tubulin binding cofactor D).
source: Signaling molecules have been found in complex with Dscam1 in Drosophila (e.g., Dock/Pak, Ableson, tubulin binding cofactor D [Okumura et al., 2015; Schmucker et al., 2000; Sterne et al., 2015]) and DSCAM in vertebrates (e.g., PAK1, FAK, Fyn [Purohit et al., 2012]).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Okumura et al., 2015; Schmucker et al., 2000; Sterne et al., 2015.

claim: Signaling molecules have been found in complex with DSCAM in vertebrates (e.g., PAK1, FAK, Fyn).
source: Signaling molecules have been found in complex with Dscam1 in Drosophila (e.g., Dock/Pak, Ableson, tubulin binding cofactor D [Okumura et al., 2015; Schmucker et al., 2000; Sterne et al., 2015]) and DSCAM in vertebrates (e.g., PAK1, FAK, Fyn [Purohit et al., 2012]).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Purohit et al., 2012.

claim: Both MAGI-2 and MAGI-3 were found to interact with DSCAM by yeast two-hybrid.
source: Both MAGI-2 and MAGI-3 were found to interact with DSCAM by yeast two-hybrid.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When transfected into HEK293T cells, both DSCAM and DSCAM-∆C protein localized to the cell surface.
source: When transfected into HEK293T cells, both DSCAM (C) and DSCAM-∆C (D) protein localized to the cell surface as revealed by live cell staining with an antibody raised against the entire extracellular domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by live cell staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased cell number from a lack of cell death can disrupt mosaic spacing in some cell types, although not as severely as Dscam-/- mutation.
source: Increased cell number from a lack of cell death can disrupt mosaic spacing in some cell types, although not as severely as Dscam-/- mutation (Keeley et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Keeley et al., 2012.

claim: Cell spacing of ipRGCs and VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells was more severely disrupted in ∆C mutants than could be explained by increased cell number alone.
source: Therefore, cell spacing of ipRGCs and VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells was more severely disrupted in ∆C mutants than could be explained by increased cell number alone.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of ∆C mutants to Bax-/- mutants shown in Figure 5.

claim: Increased cell density can contribute to abnormal spacing and dendrite fasciculation in some cell types, but is not sufficient to explain the self-avoidance deficits and especially the fasciculation of processes found Dscam-/- retinas.
source: Thus, increased cell density can contribute to abnormal spacing and dendrite fasciculation in some cell types as previously reported (Keeley et al., 2012), but is not sufficient to explain the self-avoidance deficits and especially the fasciculation of processes found Dscam-/- retinas, and to varying degrees, in ∆C mutant retinas.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of ∆C mutants to Bax-/- mutants shown in Figures 5 and 6, and by citation to Keeley et al., 2012.

claim: bNOS-positive amacrine cells are largely disorganized in Dscam mutants on a C3H background, but not in mixed C57BL/6 – BALBc strains.
source: bNOS-positive amacrine cells are largely disorganized in Dscam mutants on a C3H background, but not in mixed C57BL/6 – BALBc strains (Fuerst et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2010.

claim: DA and M1 ipRGCs provide the only clear example of co-fasciculation in Dscam-/- mutants.
source: DA and M1 ipRGCs provide the only clear example we have seen of co-fasciculation in Dscam-/-mutants (Fuerst et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: In Dscaml1-/- mice, dyad synapses displayed features reminiscent of immature synapses, including malformed ribbons and an overabundance of synaptic vesicles.
source: In Dscaml1-/- mice, these synapses displayed features reminiscent of immature synapses, including malformed ribbons and an overabundance of synaptic vesicles (Figure 7K and [Fuerst et al., 2009]).
evidence: The claim is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 7K and by citation to Fuerst et al., 2009.

claim: DSCAML1 promotes synapse maturation independent of C-terminal interactions.
source: We inspected the dyad synapses in Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas by transmission electron microscopy, and failed to detect these synaptic phenotype reminiscent of the Dscaml1-/- mice (Figure 7L–M), indicating that DSCAML1 promotes synapse maturation independent of C-terminal interactions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that dyad synapses appear normal in Dscaml1∆C/∆C retinas despite being abnormal in Dscaml1-/- retinas.

claim: VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells stratify their neurites to the ON-OFF region of the IPL between the ChAT-positive laminae in wild type mice.
source: This population stratifies its neurites to the ON-OFF region of the IPL between the ChAT-positive laminae in wild type mice (Figure 7N).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 7N.

claim: Rather than distinguishing phenotypes based on specific molecular mechanisms, the ∆C mutations distinguished cell types.
source: Contrary to our initial hypothesis, we found that rather than distinguishing phenotypes based on specific molecular mechanisms, these mutations distinguished cell types.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants as described throughout the Results section.

claim: The requirement for a PDZ-interacting C-terminus in DSCAM or DSCAML1 is variable and depends on the cell type.
source: Thus, our main conclusion from these studies is that the requirement for a PDZ-interacting C-terminus in DSCAM or DSCAML1 is variable and depends on the cell type.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants as described throughout the Results section.

claim: Dscam1 in Drosophila uses three banks of alternatively spliced exons to produce 19,008 isoforms with distinct extracellular domains.
source: Dscam1 in Drosophila uses three banks of alternatively spliced exons to produce 19,008 isoforms with distinct extracellular domains (Schmucker et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schmucker et al., 2000.

claim: Each of the three alternatively spliced exons in Dscam1 encode regions of the protein essential for homophilic binding, resulting in 19,008 potential molecules that preferentially recognize other copies of the same isoform.
source: Each of these three exons encode regions of the protein essential for homophilic binding, resulting in 19,008 potential molecules that preferentially recognize other copies of the same isoform (Sawaya et al., 2008; Wojtowicz et al., 2004, 2007; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sawaya et al., 2008; Wojtowicz et al., 2004, 2007; Wu et al., 2012.

claim: A given neuron expresses an estimated 10–50 Dscam1 isoforms, most of which will differ from neighboring neurons.
source: By biased stochastic exon choice, a given neuron expresses an estimated 10–50 isoforms, most of which will differ from neighboring neurons (Miura et al., 2013; Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Miura et al., 2013; Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004.

claim: Vast isoform diversity is required for Dscam1 to function normally.
source: As might be expected with such a mechanism in which each cell is uniquely identified, vast isoform diversity is required for Dscam1 to function normally (Hattori et al., 2009, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hattori et al., 2009, 2007.

claim: There are 22 Pcdhg isoforms, specified by alternative promoter choice within the gene cluster.
source: There are only 22 Pcdhg isoforms, specified by alternative promoter choice within the gene cluster instead of alternative splicing, but the resulting proteins form cis multimers with trans homophilic binding specificity at the multimer level (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014; Wu and Maniatis, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014; Wu and Maniatis, 1999.

claim: Pcdhg proteins form cis multimers with trans homophilic binding specificity at the multimer level.
source: There are only 22 Pcdhg isoforms, specified by alternative promoter choice within the gene cluster instead of alternative splicing, but the resulting proteins form cis multimers with trans homophilic binding specificity at the multimer level (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014; Wu and Maniatis, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014; Wu and Maniatis, 1999.

claim: PCDHG promotes self-avoidance in cerebellar Purkinje cells and retinal starburst amacrine cells.
source: PCDHG promotes self-avoidance in cerebellar Purkinje cells and retinal starburst amacrine cells (SACs) (Lefebvre et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lefebvre et al., 2012.

claim: When only one Pcdhg isoform was expressed in SACs, self-avoidance at the single cell level was preserved, but interactions between neighboring SACs were aberrant, resulting in circuit level dysfunction.
source: When only one isoform was expressed in SACs, self-avoidance at the single cell level was preserved, but interactions between neighboring SACs were aberrant, resulting in circuit level dysfunction (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015.

claim: Without extensive isoform diversity, vertebrate DSCAMs are not able to provide fine level self-recognition.
source: Without extensive isoform diversity, vertebrate DSCAMs are not able to provide this fine level of self-recognition.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison with Dscam1 and Pcdhg systems that require diversity for self/non-self discrimination.

claim: DSCAMs function through at least two molecular mechanisms, one that requires a C-terminal PDZ-interacting motif, and one that does not.
source: Our conclusion that DSCAMs function through at least two molecular mechanisms, one that requires a C-terminal PDZ-interacting motif, and one that does not, fits a model in which DSCAMs interact with cell-type-specific adhesion mechanisms to serve their function.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants.

claim: de Andrade and colleagues found little co-localization between DSCAM and seven different multi-PDZ proteins in the adult IPL.
source: de Andrade and colleagues analyzed the co-localization of DSCAM with seven different multi-PDZ proteins, including MAGI-2 and MAGI-3, and found little co-localization in the adult IPL.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to work by de Andrade and colleagues.

claim: There was increased co-localization between DSCAM and multi-PDZ proteins during development, indicating that these interactions are dynamic and transient.
source: Interestingly, there was increased co-localization during development, indicating that these interactions are dynamic and transient (de Andrade et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to de Andrade et al., 2014.

claim: Keeley and colleagues tested if cell death was the primary function in DA cells and ipRGCs, and found that while increasing cell density by inhibiting developmental cell death could contribute to spacing defects, it was not sufficient to explain the loss of self-avoidance in Dscam-/- mutants.
source: Keeley and colleagues tested if cell death was this primary function in DA cells and ipRGCs, and found that while increasing cell density by inhibiting developmental cell death could contribute to spacing defects, it was not sufficient to explain the loss of self-avoidance in Dscam-/- mutants (Keeley et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Keeley et al., 2012.

claim: Promotion of cell death is not the sole primary function of the Dscams.
source: Thus, promotion of cell death is not the sole primary function of the Dscams.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of ∆C mutants to Bax-/- mutants showing that spacing defects cannot be fully explained by increased cell density.

claim: ipRGC clustering and fasciculation occurs in Dscam-/- mutants even when cell density is severely reduced by Pou4f2 double mutation.
source: This is consistent with our previous finding that ipRGC clustering and fasciculation occurs in Dscam-/-mutants even when cell density is severely reduced by Pou4f2 double mutation (Fuerst et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fuerst et al., 2012.

claim: The molecular mechanisms through which DSCAMs function will need to be defined on a cell type by cell type basis.
source: However, what these results clearly demonstrate is that the molecular mechanisms through which DSCAMs function will need to be defined on a cell type by cell type basis, and that a single molecular complex or pathway will not account for DSCAMs' function(s) in all cell types.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential phenotypes observed across multiple cell types in the ∆C mutants.
